title: Complicated persistent structures imply moving structures exist

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Complicated persistent structures imply moving structures exist

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In class 4 cellular automata, whenever sufficiently complicated persistent structures occur, structures that move can eventually be found; moving structures are what allow information to travel and complex class 4 behavior to occur.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: My experience with many different rules is that whenever sufficiently complicated persistent structures occur, structures that move can eventually be found.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Structures in Class 4 Systems” (from p. 281), p. 286. Scope: class 4 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-23: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing catalogs can strongly test the association in well-studied systems. The threshold and eventual-findability wording prevent a decisive general test, and negative searches have weak force.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a specified class 4 rule catalog, enumerate persistent structures and classify them by internal-state complexity and displacement per period. Test whether every rule above a preregistered persistent-structure complexity threshold contains a nonzero-velocity structure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available structure catalogs heavily favor a few famous rules.

Failure to find a mover is not proof of absence.

“Sufficiently complicated” is unspecified.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.42
data existence: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.56
analysis feasibility: 0.54
data adequacy: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Spaceship searches are standard and, for Life and rule 110, already public, so particular rules can be shown to have moving objects. The sentence is an implication with an adjustable antecedent, sufficiently complicated, and an unbounded search, eventually. A finite census can add examples; it cannot close the implication or refute it by failing to find a spaceship.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In each class 4 rule with a known stationary object above a declared size, search larger seeds for a spaceship. A moving object supports the implication for that rule; a completeness proof that only stationary objects exist would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The supporting evidence is experience with many rules, not a defined sample.

Sufficiently complicated can be raised after a stationary-only example.

Eventually sets no search bound, so a negative census is inconclusive.
